views.name: race_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  raceId,
  year,
  round,
  circuitId,
  name,
  date,
  time,
  -- combine date and time when both present; NULL if time missing
  CASE
    WHEN date IS NOT NULL AND time IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(time) != '' THEN date || ' ' || time
    WHEN date IS NOT NULL THEN date
    ELSE NULL
  END AS datetime
FROM races

params.description: Provides one row per race event with basic race attributes (identifiers, timing, and location) to be used as a canonical race dimension for analysis and joins.
params.when_to_use: Looking up race-level attributes (name, date/time, circuit) for a given raceId or for a set of raceIds | Joining race metadata onto measures computed at other grains (drivers, constructors, laps, pitstops) to provide event context | Building season- or race-level reports (counts of races, timeline/listing of races, calendars) where one row per race is required | Composing higher-level queries that filter or group by year, round, circuitId, or date/datetime
params.output_schema: raceId: unique identifier of the race event (derived from races.raceId) | year: integer season/year the race belongs to (derived from races.year) | round: race round number within the season (derived from races.round) | circuitId: identifier of the circuit where the race was held (derived from races.circuitId) | name: official name of the race event (derived from races.name) | date: date of the race (derived from races.date) | time: scheduled/start time of the race as stored (derived from races.time) | datetime: combined timestamp string of date and time when both present; if time missing it equals date; NULL if date is NULL (expression: CASE ... END using races.date and races.time)
params.grounded_columns: races.raceId | races.year | races.round | races.circuitId | races.name | races.date | races.time
params.metric: datetime = CASE WHEN races.date IS NOT NULL AND races.time IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(races.time) != '' THEN races.date || ' ' || races.time WHEN races.date IS NOT NULL THEN races.date ELSE NULL END
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to driver_dim on race_basic.raceId = driver_dim.raceId — SAFE if driver_dim is implemented as one-row-per-(raceId,driverId) dimension? (Only safe if driver_dim is truly one-row-per-raceId; verify driver_dim grain before joining. If driver_dim is one-to-many per race, do NOT join directly without aggregation.) | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to constructor_dim on race_basic.circuitId = constructor_dim.circuitId — SAFE only if constructor_dim is one-row-per-circuitId. Confirm constructor_dim grain before joining. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to race_results_enriched on race_basic.raceId = race_results_enriched.raceId — NOT SAFE to join directly if you intend to preserve race-level measures, because race_results_enriched is a JOIN view that contains one row per race result (many drivers per race). Joining will multiply race_basic rows into many result rows; aggregate or filter race_results_enriched before merging if you require race-level uniqueness. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to driver_lap_aggregates, pitstop_aggregates, fastest_lap_per_race, qualifying_grid_positions, season_driver_points, season_constructor_points, driver_season_rank, driver_running_points_by_season on raceId (or year+race keys) — NOT SAFE to join directly if those sibling views are one-to-many (aggregates may be per driver or per lap); instead, pre-aggregate or reduce to one row per race (for race-level metrics) before joining to avoid duplicating race_basic rows/measures. | safe pattern: when combining race_basic with one-to-many views, either (a) aggregate the one-to-many view to the race_basic grain (one row per raceId) before joining, or (b) join race_basic to the many-side and then re-aggregate the result grouping by race_basic columns. This prevents measure multiplication. | explicit example: to get number_of_results per race, aggregate race_results_enriched: SELECT raceId, COUNT(*) AS num_results FROM race_results_enriched GROUP BY raceId; then join that single-row-per-race result to race_basic on raceId — safe because counts are computed prior to the join. | note on keys: primary key (grain) of this view is race_basic.raceId (one row per race event). Any join that preserves this 1:1 (or many:1 where race_basic is the many side) relationship will not duplicate race_basic rows; avoid joining race_basic (1) to tables that are many per race without pre-aggregation.

views.description: Normalized race header rows with explicit datetime and preserved race identifiers. Use this to join event/date info to results, standings, lap times, qualifying, etc. | Use for: List races in a season or between dates; Join race metadata to results/qualifying/standings; Filter events by circuit, round, or date/time

views.name: driver_dim
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  driverId,
  driverRef,
  number,
  code,
  forename,
  surname,
  dob,
  nationality,
  url
FROM drivers

params.description: Dimension of drivers — one row per driver, exposing identifying attributes and static metadata for use in filtering, labeling, and joining to driver-centric facts.
params.when_to_use: Look up driver attributes (name, nationality, date of birth, reference codes) for display or filtering. | Join driver attributes onto driver-level or driver-season-level metrics (points, ranks, aggregates) without repeating driver rows. | Compose driver-centric analytic queries (e.g., top drivers by points, average stint times by driver) by joining this view to aggregated measures keyed by driverId. | Provide the driver side of a join when building reporting tables, dashboards, or further SQL that needs driver metadata.
params.output_schema: driverId: integer — unique driver identifier; sourced from drivers.driverId | driverRef: text — short reference code/string for the driver; sourced from drivers.driverRef | number: integer/null — racing number assigned to driver (may be null); sourced from drivers.number | code: text/null — short three-letter code for the driver (may be null); sourced from drivers.code | forename: text — driver's forename; sourced from drivers.forename | surname: text — driver's surname; sourced from drivers.surname | dob: date/null — date of birth (may be null); sourced from drivers.dob | nationality: text/null — nationality string (may be null); sourced from drivers.nationality | url: text/null — external reference URL for the driver (may be null); sourced from drivers.url
params.grounded_columns: drivers.driverId | drivers.driverRef | drivers.number | drivers.code | drivers.forename | drivers.surname | drivers.dob | drivers.nationality | drivers.url
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to season_driver_points on driverId (season_driver_points.driverId = driver_dim.driverId) — safe because driver_dim is one-row-per-driver, and season_driver_points is an aggregated table keyed by driverId (and likely season); joining preserves the aggregated measures without duplication when joined on matching driverId (+ season if applicable). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to driver_season_rank on driverId (and season if required) — safe because driver_season_rank is a ranking/aggregate per driver (and season) and will not duplicate driver_dim rows for the same driver-season key. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to driver_lap_aggregates on driverId (and optionally raceId/session identifiers) — safe when driver_lap_aggregates is already aggregated by driverId (and the additional keys used) because aggregation prevents multiplication of measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to pitstop_aggregates on driverId (and raceId/session) — safe when pitstop_aggregates is aggregated by driverId (and any additional keys used) so measures remain correct. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to race_results_enriched on driverId (and raceId) only when race_results_enriched is at most one row per (driverId, raceId) and you intend to expand driver rows to per-race results; this will multiply driver_dim rows by the number of races for that driver (expected) — which is correct if the goal is per-driver-per-race analysis but not if you want to preserve one-row-per-driver. | DO NOT join driver_dim directly to non-aggregated one-to-many tables/views (for example raw lap tables, pitstop detail tables, or qualifying laps) without first aggregating those tables to the desired grain (e.g., per driver, per race) — such joins will multiply driver_dim rows and will duplicate any measures derived from driver_dim. | When composing further aggregates: if you join a one-to-many fact to driver_dim and then aggregate, ensure you aggregate only the fact measures (e.g., SUM, COUNT) after the join and not rely on driver_dim for measure calculations. Prefer joining driver_dim to already-aggregated facts (AGG views listed) to avoid accidental over-counting. | Examples of safe join keys: driver_dim.driverId = season_driver_points.driverId; driver_dim.driverId = driver_lap_aggregates.driverId; driver_dim.driverId = pitstop_aggregates.driverId; include seasonId/raceId when using season- or race-level aggregates to avoid accidental cross-season/race fan-out.

views.description: Canonical driver dimension exposing identity and birth date/nationality for joins and demographic filtering. | Use for: Find drivers by nationality or birth year; Join driver names to results, lapTimes, pitStops, qualifying
validated_on: For the Bahrain Grand Prix in 2007, how many drivers not finished the game?
counter_examples: What is his number of the driver who finished 0:01:54 in the Q3 of qualifying race No.903?
For all the drivers who finished the game in race No. 592, who is the oldest?
For all the drivers who finished the game in race No. 872, who is the youngest?
Which was Lewis Hamilton first race? What was his points recorded for his first race event?

views.name: constructor_dim
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  constructorId,
  constructorRef,
  name,
  nationality,
  url
FROM constructors

params.description: Dimension of constructors (one row per constructor) providing identifier and descriptive attributes.
params.when_to_use: Look up constructor attributes (name, reference, nationality, URL) by constructorId or constructorRef. | Join constructor descriptive data onto fact/aggregate views (race results, points, laps) to label constructor-level metrics. | Filter or group by constructor attributes when computing metrics at constructor grain (after ensuring correct cardinality). | Build higher-level constructor-side aggregations (season constructor points, race-level constructor metrics) by joining this dim to aggregated/joined fact views.
params.output_schema: constructorId: unique integer identifier for the constructor — derived from constructors.constructorId | constructorRef: short string reference/code for the constructor — derived from constructors.constructorRef | name: full constructor name — derived from constructors.name | nationality: constructor nationality label — derived from constructors.nationality | url: reference URL for the constructor — derived from constructors.url
params.metric: No derived metrics in this view; all outputs are base descriptive columns mapped 1:1 to constructors table columns.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to race_results_enriched on constructorId — safe because constructor_dim has one row per constructor (constructor_dim.constructorId = race_results_enriched.constructorId) and race_results_enriched is many-per-constructor. This attaches constructor attributes without duplicating constructor_dim rows or its measures (there are no measures in this dim). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to season_constructor_points on constructorId — safe because season_constructor_points is aggregated at (season, constructorId) or similar and will not duplicate constructor_dim rows; use constructor_dim.constructorId = season_constructor_points.constructorId to label season-level constructor metrics. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to driver_dim on no key (not recommended) or via intermediary tables only if semantically correct. Do not join constructor_dim directly to driver_dim expecting one-to-one mapping because multiple drivers map to the same constructor over time. | unsafe join caution: do NOT join constructor_dim to one-to-many fact tables (e.g., race_results_enriched, driver_lap_aggregates, pitstop_aggregates, fastest_lap_per_race, qualifying_grid_positions) and treat the result as still at constructor grain without re-aggregation. Those views are many-per-constructor; joining them to this dim will produce multiple rows per constructor (multiplying any constructor-level measures) unless you re-aggregate after the join. | safe composition pattern: to compute constructor-level metrics, first aggregate measures in the fact view to the constructor grain (e.g., SUM(points) GROUP BY constructorId, season) producing an AGG view (like season_constructor_points), then join that aggregated result to constructor_dim on constructorId to attach descriptive attributes without duplicating measures. | key guidance: use constructor_dim.constructorId as the join key for correctness — constructorRef can be used only if the downstream object is keyed by constructorRef and uniqueness is guaranteed.

views.description: Constructor/team dimension for joins and grouping in performance queries. | Use for: Aggregate points by constructor; List constructors by nationality; Join constructor attributes to results/standings

views.name: race_results_enriched
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.resultId,
  r.raceId,
  r.driverId,
  r.constructorId,
  r.number,
  r.grid,
  r.position,
  r.positionText,
  r.positionOrder,
  r.points,
  r.laps,
  r.time,
  r.milliseconds,
  r.fastestLap,
  r.rank AS rank,
  r.fastestLapTime,
  r.fastestLapSpeed,
  r.statusId,
  ra.year,
  ra.round,
  ra.circuitId,
  ra.name AS name,
  ra.date,
  ra.time AS time_of_race,
  d.forename,
  d.surname,
  d.code,
  d.number AS driver_number,
  d.nationality AS driver_nationality,
  c.name AS constructor_name,
  c.nationality AS constructor_nationality,
  s.status AS status
FROM results r
LEFT JOIN races ra ON r.raceId = ra.raceId
LEFT JOIN drivers d ON r.driverId = d.driverId
LEFT JOIN constructors c ON r.constructorId = c.constructorId
LEFT JOIN status s ON r.statusId = s.statusId
grain: resultId (one row per race result entry)

params.description: Row-level enriched race results combining results with race, driver, constructor and status attributes (one row per resultId).
params.when_to_use: Get detailed information for individual race results (e.g., points, finishing position, times) enriched with race, driver and constructor attributes. | Filter or aggregate race outcomes by season, round, circuit, driver, constructor, status, or race-level attributes. | Use as the base for season-, driver-, or constructor-level aggregations when starting from individual results (one row per resultId). | Join to one-row lookup/dimension tables (drivers, constructors, races, status) to add descriptive attributes without duplicating measures.
params.output_schema: resultId: Primary key of this view's grain — unique identifier for the race result row; derived from results.resultId. | raceId: Identifier of the race for this result; derived from results.raceId. | driverId: Identifier of the driver for this result; derived from results.driverId. | constructorId: Identifier of the constructor for this result; derived from results.constructorId. | number: Car number as recorded in results.number (may be NULL). | grid: Starting grid position from results.grid. | position: Finishing position as recorded in results.position (string, may be 'R'/'DQ' etc). | positionText: Textual finishing position from results.positionText (often same as position but preserved as text). | positionOrder: Numeric ordering of finishing position from results.positionOrder (useful for ordering results). | points: Championship points awarded for this result from results.points (numeric measure). | laps: Number of laps completed from results.laps (integer). | time: Official race time/duration string from results.time (free text). | milliseconds: Official race time in milliseconds from results.milliseconds (numeric, NULL if not recorded). | fastestLap: Fastest lap number achieved by this result from results.fastestLap (integer or NULL). | rank: Rank associated with the fastest lap or classification from results.rank (as selected in SQL: r.rank). | fastestLapTime: Fastest lap time string from results.fastestLapTime. | fastestLapSpeed: Fastest lap speed numeric (results.fastestLapSpeed). | statusId: Foreign key to status table from results.statusId. | year: Season year for the race from races.year (derived via races table join on raceId). | round: Round number of the race from races.round. | circuitId: Identifier of the circuit where the race was held from races.circuitId. | name: Race name/from races.name (aliased as name). | date: Race date from races.date. | time_of_race: Race time from races.time (aliased as time_of_race to avoid collision with results.time). | forename: Driver forename from drivers.forename (joined via driverId). | surname: Driver surname from drivers.surname. | code: Driver short code from drivers.code. | driver_number: Driver historic/permanent number from drivers.number (aliased driver_number). | driver_nationality: Driver nationality from drivers.nationality. | constructor_name: Constructor full name from constructors.name. | constructor_nationality: Constructor nationality from constructors.nationality. | status: Human readable status label from status.status (joined via statusId).
params.grounded_columns: results.resultId | results.raceId | results.driverId | results.constructorId | results.number | results.grid | results.position | results.positionText | results.positionOrder | results.points | results.laps | results.time | results.milliseconds | results.fastestLap | results.rank | results.fastestLapTime | results.fastestLapSpeed | results.statusId | races.year | races.round | races.circuitId | races.name | races.date | races.time | drivers.forename | drivers.surname | drivers.code | drivers.number | drivers.nationality | constructors.name | constructors.nationality | status.status
params.metric: points = results.points (numeric award per result; not aggregated in this view — use SUM(points) when aggregating over groups). | laps = results.laps (per-row lap count; aggregate with SUM or AVG as needed). | milliseconds = results.milliseconds (per-row time in ms; aggregate with MIN/MAX/AVG depending on intent). | fastestLapSpeed = results.fastestLapSpeed (per-row fastest lap speed; aggregate with MAX/AVG as needed).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to driver_dim (or drivers) on driverId — safe because race_results_enriched is already one row per resultId and drivers/driver_dim are one-row-per-driver; joining will not duplicate result-level measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to constructor_dim (or constructors) on constructorId — safe because constructors is one-row-per-constructor; joining will not duplicate this view's measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to race_basic (or races) on raceId — safe because races is one-row-per-race; joining will not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to status on statusId — safe because status is a lookup (one row per statusId). | do NOT join to one-to-many aggregate/detail tables (without re-aggregation) such as driver_lap_aggregates, pitstop_aggregates, fastest_lap_per_race, qualifying_grid_positions, driver_running_points_by_season, season_driver_points, season_constructor_points, or driver_season_rank if those views are many-rows-per-resultId or many-rows-per-race/driver: such joins can multiply rows and therefore duplicate per-result measures (points, laps, milliseconds). Instead: |  - To combine with a one-to-many view (e.g., pitstop_aggregates which may have multiple pitstops per result/driver/race), first aggregate that view to the same grain (resultId or driverId+raceId) and then join on the shared key. |  - To compute composite metrics (e.g., total pitstop time per result), aggregate pitstop_aggregates to resultId and then LEFT JOIN on resultId; use SUM/AVG on the aggregated columns so the result-level points/laps are not multiplied. |  - When joining to driver-level season aggregates (season_driver_points, driver_season_rank) that are one-row-per-driver-per-season, join on driverId AND year (race year) — this is safe because those aggregates are one-row-per-(driver,year). |  - When joining to fastest_lap_per_race (one-row-per-race or one-row-per-race-driver depending on its grain), ensure the join keys match its grain: if it is one-row-per-race, join on raceId; if one-row-per-race-driver, join on raceId+driverId. Confirm the sibling view's documented grain before joining. | explanation of duplication risk: this view's measures (points, laps, milliseconds) are stored per resultId. Any join to a table/view that has multiple rows per resultId (or per the same join key) will cause those measures to be duplicated unless the joined table is pre-aggregated to one row per resultId or the result measures are re-aggregated after the join (for example, SUM(points) GROUP BY resultId will be inflated if points were duplicated). | recommended planner behavior: prefer joining to one-row-per-(key) dimension tables directly; for many-to-one or many-to-many sources, perform aggregation/subquery to the one-row-per-resultId (this view's grain) before joining, or perform result-level aggregations after the join using DISTINCT keys or grouping that re-computes measures correctly.

views.description: Denormalized results rows joined to races, drivers and constructors. Useful as a single wide table for filtering, aggregations, and ranking across race results. | Use for: Compare driver/constructor performance in a race or season; Filter results by position, points, status; Build leaderboards or time-based analyses using result milliseconds

views.name: driver_lap_aggregates
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  raceId,
  driverId,
  COUNT(*) AS lap_count,
  MIN(milliseconds) AS best_lap_ms,
  MAX(milliseconds) AS worst_lap_ms,
  AVG(milliseconds) AS avg_lap_ms
FROM lapTimes
GROUP BY raceId, driverId

params.description: Per-race, per-driver lap time aggregates: count, best, worst, and average lap duration in milliseconds.
params.when_to_use: Determine how many laps a driver completed in a specific race (lap_count). | Compare drivers in a race by best, worst, or average lap time (best_lap_ms, worst_lap_ms, avg_lap_ms). | Compose race-level or driver-level reports that need per-driver lap summaries as inputs to further aggregation (e.g., season aggregates, ranks, or joins to results). | Filter drivers by lap performance (e.g., avg_lap_ms < X) before joining to other dimensions or results.
params.output_schema: raceId: identifier of the race grouping key — derived directly from lapTimes.raceId (GROUP BY key). | driverId: identifier of the driver grouping key — derived directly from lapTimes.driverId (GROUP BY key). | lap_count: number of lapTimes rows for this (raceId, driverId) — derived as COUNT(*) on lapTimes (counts laps recorded). | best_lap_ms: fastest lap time (minimum milliseconds) for this (raceId, driverId) — derived as MIN(milliseconds) from lapTimes. | worst_lap_ms: slowest lap time (maximum milliseconds) for this (raceId, driverId) — derived as MAX(milliseconds) from lapTimes. | avg_lap_ms: average lap time (mean of milliseconds) for this (raceId, driverId) — derived as AVG(milliseconds) from lapTimes.
params.metric: lap_count = COUNT(*) over rows in lapTimes grouped by (lapTimes.raceId, lapTimes.driverId) | best_lap_ms = MIN(lapTimes.milliseconds) over rows in lapTimes grouped by (lapTimes.raceId, lapTimes.driverId) | worst_lap_ms = MAX(lapTimes.milliseconds) over rows in lapTimes grouped by (lapTimes.raceId, lapTimes.driverId) | avg_lap_ms = AVG(lapTimes.milliseconds) over rows in lapTimes grouped by (lapTimes.raceId, lapTimes.driverId)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to race_basic on raceId — safe because race_basic is one-row-per-race; joining will not duplicate AGG measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to driver_dim on driverId — safe because driver_dim is one-row-per-driver; joining will not duplicate AGG measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to constructor_dim via driver or results (if a single constructor per driver-season mapping exists and you ensure join keys are unique) — only safe when the target is one-row-per-key; otherwise re-aggregate after the join. | DO NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views such as pitstop_aggregates, fastest_lap_per_race, qualifying_grid_positions, race_results_enriched, season_driver_points, season_constructor_points, driver_season_rank, driver_running_points_by_season, or lapTimes itself without re-aggregation — these joins can multiply rows and therefore duplicate lap_count and distort best/worst/avg metrics. | If you must combine with a one-to-many dataset (e.g., pitstop_aggregates which may have multiple pit rows per driver/race aggregation or race_results_enriched which can be many rows per race/driver depending on enrichment), perform one of the following safe patterns: | - Pre-aggregate the one-to-many side to one-row-per (raceId, driverId) before joining, or | - Join and then re-aggregate the numeric measures, e.g., compute SUM(lap_count) or recompute MIN/MAX/AVG from raw milliseconds after joining to avoid double-counting. | When composing into higher-level aggregates (e.g., season-level driver aggregates), aggregate this view by driverId and season (join to race_basic to get season) using SUM(lap_count) and appropriate aggregates for best/worst/avg (e.g., MIN(best_lap_ms) for season best, MAX(worst_lap_ms) for season worst, weighted AVG if weighting by laps is desired: SUM(avg_lap_ms * lap_count) / SUM(lap_count)). | Notes on AVG composition: avg_lap_ms is a per-(race,driver) mean. To compute a correct combined average across multiple races, use a weighted average with lap_count as weights (do not average avg_lap_ms naïvely).

views.description: Aggregated lap-time measures per driver per race (count, best/worst/avg milliseconds). Useful for comparing consistency and pace within a race or across races. | Use for: Find fastest lap per driver in a race; Compare average lap times between drivers or races; Detect drivers with missing lap records (lap_count smaller than expected)

views.name: pitstop_aggregates
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  raceId,
  driverId,
  COUNT(*) AS pit_count,
  SUM(milliseconds) AS total_pit_ms,
  AVG(milliseconds) AS avg_pit_ms
FROM pitStops
GROUP BY raceId, driverId

params.description: Per-race, per-driver pit stop aggregates: counts, total time, and average time of pit stops in a race.
params.when_to_use: How many pit stops did a specific driver make in a particular race? | What was the total pit stop time (milliseconds) for a driver in a race? | What was the average pit stop duration (milliseconds) for a driver in a race? | Compose with race or driver dimensions to report pit stop metrics by season, circuit, team, or driver attributes (ensure aggregation or safe joins as described). | Join into race-level or driver-level summaries (after re-aggregation) to include pit metrics per race-driver combination.
params.output_schema: raceId: race identifier — derived directly from pitStops.raceId (GROUP BY key) | driverId: driver identifier — derived directly from pitStops.driverId (GROUP BY key) | pit_count: number of pit stop records for this raceId+driverId — derived as COUNT(*) over pitStops rows for the group | total_pit_ms: sum of pit stop durations (milliseconds) for this raceId+driverId — derived as SUM(pitStops.milliseconds) | avg_pit_ms: average pit stop duration (milliseconds) for this raceId+driverId — derived as AVG(pitStops.milliseconds)
params.metric: pit_count = COUNT(*)  -- count of pitStops rows per (pitStops.raceId, pitStops.driverId) | total_pit_ms = SUM(pitStops.milliseconds)  -- sum of milliseconds per (raceId, driverId) | avg_pit_ms = AVG(pitStops.milliseconds)  -- average milliseconds per (raceId, driverId)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to race_basic on raceId — safe because race_basic is one-row-per-race; joining AGG (one-row-per raceId+driverId) to race_basic will not duplicate AGG measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to driver_dim on driverId — safe because driver_dim is one-row-per-driver; joining AGG to driver_dim will not duplicate AGG measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to constructor_dim on constructorId only after first joining AGG to a single-row-per-driver mapping (e.g., driver_dim with constructorId) — direct join to constructor_dim requires a one-to-one key to avoid duplication. | DO NOT join AGG directly to one-to-many views/tables (for example: driver_lap_aggregates, fastest_lap_per_race, qualifying_grid_positions, season_driver_points, season_constructor_points, driver_running_points_by_season) without re-aggregation or ensuring uniqueness because those are not one-row-per-(raceId,driverId) and will multiply AGG's measures. If you must combine, either: |   - Aggregate the one-to-many side to the same grain (raceId, driverId) before joining, or |   - Join and then re-aggregate grouping by the desired grain (e.g., raceId, driverId) to restore correct sums/counts. | Examples of safe compositions: |   - To get pit metrics with race attributes: SELECT ... FROM pitstop_aggregates AGG JOIN race_basic R ON AGG.raceId = R.raceId |   - To get pit metrics with driver attributes: SELECT ... FROM pitstop_aggregates AGG JOIN driver_dim D ON AGG.driverId = D.driverId | Examples of unsafe compositions without re-aggregation: |   - AGG JOIN driver_lap_aggregates (one-to-many per raceId+driverId) — will duplicate pit_count and total_pit_ms unless you aggregate the joined result back to (raceId, driverId). | Notes on planner behavior: treat pitstop_aggregates as materialized at grain (raceId, driverId). Any join that preserves one row per (raceId, driverId) is safe; any join that expands rows per (raceId, driverId) requires re-aggregation to avoid inflating COUNT/SUM metrics.

views.description: Aggregated pit stop metrics per driver per race (count, total/avg milliseconds). Useful to analyze pit strategy and time lost in pits. | Use for: Compare pit stop frequency and total pit time between drivers; Correlate pit stop time with race position changes

views.name: season_driver_points
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.year,
  res.driverId,
  SUM(res.points) AS season_points,
  COUNT(DISTINCT res.raceId) AS races_participated
FROM results res
JOIN races r ON res.raceId = r.raceId
GROUP BY r.year, res.driverId

params.description: Season-level aggregated driver points and participation: total points and number of races a driver participated in for each year.
params.when_to_use: Get each driver's total championship points and how many races they participated in for a given season (year). | Rank or compare drivers within a season by total points or races participated. | Join season-level driver points to driver attributes (name, nationality) or constructor-level season results for reporting, dashboards, or further aggregation to championship-level metrics. | Use as the aggregation source when composing more complex season-level analyses (e.g., points per race, correlation with qualifying) without re-aggregating raw results.
params.output_schema: year: championship year (from races.year) | driverId: unique identifier of the driver (from results.driverId) | season_points: SUM(res.points) — total points the driver scored in that year (derived from results.points aggregated per year, driver) | races_participated: COUNT(DISTINCT res.raceId) — number of distinct races the driver had a result in that year (derived from results.raceId aggregated per year, driver)

params.composition: SAFE: Join to driver_dim on driver_dim.driverId = season_driver_points.driverId — safe because season_driver_points has one row per (year, driverId); joining to the driver dimension (one row per driver) will not duplicate season measures. | SAFE: Join to driver_season_rank on (driver_season_rank.year = season_driver_points.year AND driver_season_rank.driverId = season_driver_points.driverId) — safe because driver_season_rank is expected to be one-row-per (year, driverId) rank information. | SAFE: Join to season_constructor_points only when joining via constructor-specific keys (e.g., year + constructorId) and after aggregating or filtering appropriately; direct join on year alone is safe for adding season-level constructor metrics but will not match driver rows unless you also supply a constructorId key. | UNSAFE: Do NOT directly join to race_results_enriched, qualifying_grid_positions, driver_lap_aggregates, pitstop_aggregates, fastest_lap_per_race, or any other one-to-many-per-(year,driver) detail table/view without re-aggregation — those joins would multiply season_points and races_participated because those sources contain multiple rows per race or per driver within the same year. | UNSAFE: Do NOT join to races (the raw races table) or results (the raw results table) on raceId without re-aggregating, as those are many-to-one or many-to-many relative to this view's (year, driverId) grain and will duplicate aggregated measures. | GUIDANCE: If you need additional row-level detail (e.g., per-race metrics) join season_driver_points to a per-race-per-driver table (like race_results_enriched) only after either (a) aggregating that table to the season level keyed by (year, driverId), or (b) distributing the season measures proportionally by some denominator (e.g., points per race = season_points / races_participated) computed in SQL to avoid double-counting. | GUIDANCE: When composing to higher-level aggregations (e.g., total points for all drivers in a year), you can safely aggregate season_driver_points across driverId because it is at driver-season grain; use SUM(season_points) grouped by year to get championship total points across drivers.

params.description: Per-constructor, per-year aggregated season points and count of distinct races participated (season-level constructor performance totals).
params.when_to_use: Report total constructor points in a given season (year) or across seasons. | Rank or compare constructors by season_points within a year. | Compute per-season averages or ratios that use constructor-level season totals (e.g., points per race for a constructor in a year). | As a building block when composing season-level constructor metrics into larger dashboards (join to constructor details or year-level calendars).
params.output_schema: year: the season year (derived from races.year). | constructorId: the constructor identifier (derived from results.constructorId). | season_points: total sum of points earned by that constructor in that year (derived as SUM(results.points)). | races_participated: number of distinct races that constructor scored points or had result rows in that year (derived as COUNT(DISTINCT results.raceId)).
params.metric: season_points = SUM(results.points)  -- aggregate of results.points grouped by (races.year, results.constructorId) | races_participated = COUNT(DISTINCT results.raceId)  -- distinct count of race occurrences for the constructor within the year
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to constructor_dim on constructorId — safe because this view is one-row-per (year, constructorId). Enriches with constructor attributes without duplicating season_points or races_participated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a year or season dimension (e.g., a calendar/year table keyed by year) on year — safe because it's one-row-per year-constructor combination and will not duplicate aggregates when joined to one-row-per-year dimension. | DO NOT join directly to results (or any other table/view that is one-to-many per constructorId within the same year) without re-aggregation, e.g., joining to results, race_results_enriched, driver_lap_aggregates, pitstop_aggregates, qualifying_grid_positions, fastest_lap_per_race, driver_running_points_by_season, or any per-race/per-driver detail: those joins are many-to-one (many detail rows per this view's row) and will multiply season_points and races_participated unless you re-aggregate after the join or join on a pre-aggregated sibling keyed at the same grain. | If you need to combine this view with race-level or driver-level details, either: (a) aggregate the detail to the same grain (year, constructorId) before joining, or (b) join in a derived subquery that computes metrics at the (year, constructorId) grain — this prevents measure duplication. | Safe composition with sibling AGG views: you may join to other aggregated views that are keyed at (year, constructorId) (if present) without duplication. Do NOT join to aggregated views keyed at a finer grain (e.g., per-race or per-driver) unless those views are re-aggregated to (year, constructorId) first. | When composing into higher-level metrics (e.g., points per race = season_points / races_participated), compute those expressions using the columns from this view directly; avoid recalculating using joined detail rows which could change denominators/numerators due to duplication.

views.name: driver_season_rank
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  sp.year,
  sp.driverId,
  sp.season_points,
  sp.races_participated,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sp.year ORDER BY sp.season_points DESC) AS season_rank
FROM (
  SELECT
    r.year,
    res.driverId,
    SUM(res.points) AS season_points,
    COUNT(DISTINCT res.raceId) AS races_participated
  FROM results res
  JOIN races r ON res.raceId = r.raceId
  GROUP BY r.year, res.driverId
) sp
grain: year, driverId (one row per driver per season with rank)

params.description: Per-season rank and participation summary for each driver (one row per driver per year), ranking drivers within each season by total season points.
params.when_to_use: Find a driver's rank within a specific season or across seasons (e.g., Who was the 2016 champion?). | Compare drivers' season-level performance by points and number of races participated. | Build season-level leaderboards, filters, or visualizations that require one row per driver-season with an ordinal rank. | As a building block (seed) for composing higher-level season analytics that need driver season aggregates and stable cardinality.
params.output_schema: year: the season year (sourced from races.year) | driverId: unique identifier of the driver (sourced from results.driverId) | season_points: total points the driver scored during that year (derived as SUM(results.points) grouped by year and driverId) | races_participated: number of distinct races the driver participated in that year (derived as COUNT(DISTINCT results.raceId) grouped by year and driverId) | season_rank: integer rank for the driver within the year, computed by RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY year ORDER BY season_points DESC) (ties receive the same rank and gaps may occur)
params.metric: season_points = SUM(results.points)  -- aggregated per (races.year, results.driverId) | races_participated = COUNT(DISTINCT results.raceId)  -- aggregated per (races.year, results.driverId) | season_rank = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY year ORDER BY season_points DESC)  -- computed on the aggregated per-driver-per-year rows
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to driver_dim on driverId — safe because driver_dim is one-row-per-driver (joining preserves one row per driver-season; season_points and races_participated are not duplicated). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to race_basic or season_constructor_points only when joining on year (e.g., to bring season-level attributes) — safe if those are one-row-per-year; confirm their grains before joining. | do NOT join this view directly to race_results_enriched, results, or any other one-to-many detail table (e.g., lap-level tables, pitstop_aggregates at race or lap grain) without re-aggregation — those joins would duplicate the season_points and races_participated measures because driver_season_rank is already aggregated to driver-season grain. | do NOT join to driver_lap_aggregates, pitstop_aggregates, fastest_lap_per_race, qualifying_grid_positions, or any view whose grain is one-or-more rows per (race or driver-race) without first aggregating that view to driver-season (matching year + driverId) — otherwise the season aggregates will be multiplied by the number of matching lower-grain rows. | If you need to combine driver_season_rank with another view that has a many-rows-per-driver-per-season grain (e.g., race-level or lap-level data), first aggregate that view to the same grain (group by year, driverId) producing metrics like SUM(metric) or COUNT(DISTINCT raceId) as appropriate, then join on (year, driverId) to preserve correct measures. | When composing additional metrics that should be ranked or used in ORDER BY for ties, prefer recomputing window functions after any joins/aggregations to ensure rankings reflect the final combined measures and avoid relying on season_rank if underlying measures were changed by composition.

views.description: Season ranking of drivers by season points with ties handled by RANK(); outputs rank per driver per year. Use this to select top-K drivers per season by filtering on rank. | Use for: Top-K drivers per season; Track rank progression across seasons (join by driverId)

views.name: fastest_lap_per_race
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  lt_min.raceId,
  lt_min.best_lap_ms,
  lt.driverId,
  lt.lap,
  lt.time AS time,
  lt.position
FROM (
  SELECT raceId, MIN(milliseconds) AS best_lap_ms
  FROM lapTimes
  GROUP BY raceId
) lt_min
JOIN lapTimes lt
  ON lt.raceId = lt_min.raceId
  AND lt.milliseconds = lt_min.best_lap_ms
grain: raceId, driverId, lap (one row per driver lap matching the race fastest lap; may be multiple if tie)

params.description: Fastest lap(s) per race: for each race, the minimum lap time in milliseconds and the driver lap rows that match that minimum (ties allowed).
params.when_to_use: Find which driver(s) set the fastest lap in each race and the lap details (lap number, reported time, position) for those laps. | Filter races by fastest-lap performance (e.g., find races where fastest lap < X ms) or join to race/driver dimensions to report contextual details (season, circuit, driver name). | Compose into season- or driver-level summaries when counting fastest-lap occurrences per driver/season (requires re-aggregation after joining).
params.output_schema: raceId: race identifier — sourced from lapTimes.raceId (GROUP BY key in the inner aggregation and returned from lt.raceId). | best_lap_ms: race-level metric — MIN(milliseconds) from lapTimes for that race; sourced from the inner aggregation (lt_min.best_lap_ms). | driverId: driver identifier for the lap row that matches the race's best_lap_ms — sourced from lapTimes.driverId (lt.driverId). | lap: lap number for the matching lap row — sourced from lapTimes.lap (lt.lap). | time: reported time string for the matching lap row — sourced from lapTimes.time (lt.time). | position: race position value recorded for that lap row — sourced from lapTimes.position (lt.position).
params.grounded_columns: lapTimes.raceId | lapTimes.milliseconds | lapTimes.driverId | lapTimes.lap | lapTimes.time | lapTimes.position
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to race_basic on raceId — safe because fastest_lap_per_race has at most one row per (raceId, driverId, lap) for the fastest-lap rows; when race_basic is 1:1 per raceId, joining will not multiply the race-level best_lap_ms metric. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to driver_dim on driverId — safe because driver_dim is expected to be 1:1 per driverId, so joining will not duplicate fastest-lap rows/measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to constructor_dim via driver/entry keys only if the constructor_dim is 1:1 per the key you join on; otherwise ensure you join on a unique constructor key to avoid duplication. | DO NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views such as race_results_enriched, driver_lap_aggregates, pitstop_aggregates, season_driver_points, season_constructor_points, driver_season_rank, qualifying_grid_positions, or driver_running_points_by_season without re-aggregation or deduplication first — these are one-to-many relative to a race or driver and would multiply rows and thus multiply the implied count/occurrence of fastest-lap rows. If you need aggregated measures from those siblings, first aggregate them to the same grain (raceId or raceId+driverId) and then join. | If you need counts of fastest laps per driver/season, aggregate this view after joining to race_basic (to get season) or to driver_dim: e.g., GROUP BY driverId, season, COUNT(*) AS fastest_lap_count — do not rely on implicit de-duplication by joining this view to non-unique tables. | If multiple rows per race are acceptable (ties), be aware the view intentionally returns all tied fastest laps. If you require a single canonical fastest-lap driver per race, apply a deterministic tie-breaker (e.g., MIN(driverId)) in a downstream aggregation before joining to 1:1 dimensions.

views.description: Fastest lap (minimum milliseconds) per race with driver(s) who set it. Useful to find the single best lap in each race and associated drivers. | Use for: Who set the fastest lap in each race; Compare fastest lap times across races or drivers

params.description: Row-level qualifying session data per qualifyId (one row per qualifying entry) linking qualifying times and positions to race, driver and constructor context.

joining to a race table (one row per raceId) will not duplicate qualifying rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to driver_dim on driverId — safe because drivers is one row per driverId; this is a many (qualify rows) to one (driver) join and will not duplicate qualifying measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to constructor_dim on constructorId — safe because constructors is one row per constructorId; this will not duplicate qualifying measures. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many detail/aggregate tables (for example driver_lap_aggregates, pitstop_aggregates, fastest_lap_per_race, race_results_enriched) without handling cardinality — those are one-to-many relative to qualifyId or raceId and will multiply rows/measures from this view unless you either: | - aggregate the one-to-many table to the same grain (qualifyId or raceId or driverId) before joining, or | - join via a subquery that selects a single row per key (e.g., latest/aggregate value per raceId or driverId), or | - join using EXISTS/IN or lateral (apply) patterns that do not inflate row counts. | Examples of unsafe joins unless re-aggregated: joining driver_lap_aggregates (aggregated per lap segments) or pitstop_aggregates (multiple pitstops per driver/race) directly to this view on (raceId, driverId) would multiply qualify rows because those sources are many-per-(raceId,driverId). | If you need season-level metrics (season_driver_points, season_constructor_points, driver_season_rank), first aggregate qualifying_grid_positions by driverId and year (or join to the season-level table on driverId+year) ensuring the season table is one-row-per-(driver,year) to avoid duplication. | When composing sums/averages of qualifying measures across this view (e.g., average q1 by driver), compute the aggregation from this view (group by driverId) rather than joining per-lap or per-pitstop details which would require de-duplication.

views.name: driver_running_points_by_season
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  sp.year,
  sp.driverId,
  sp.raceId,
  sp.race_date,
  sp.points_in_race,
  SUM(sp.points_in_race) OVER (PARTITION BY sp.year, sp.driverId ORDER BY sp.race_date, sp.raceId ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_season_points
FROM (
  SELECT
    r.year,
    res.driverId,
    res.raceId,
    r.date AS race_date,
    SUM(res.points) AS points_in_race
  FROM results res
  JOIN races r ON res.raceId = r.raceId
  GROUP BY r.year, res.driverId, res.raceId, r.date
) sp
grain: year, driverId, raceId (one row per driver per race with cumulative season points up to that race)

params.description: Per-driver, per-race cumulative season points up to that race (one row per driver per race with running total of points in the season).
params.when_to_use: Show a driver's cumulative championship points after each race in a season | Plot a driver's season points progression across race dates | Compare multiple drivers' running season points at the same race | Compose season-level aggregates (e.g., final season points) by taking the max running_season_points per driver per year | Build driver ranking by points at any race by ranking running_season_points within a race
params.output_schema: year: calendar year of the race (derived from races.year) | driverId: unique identifier of the driver (derived from results.driverId) | raceId: unique identifier of the race (derived from results.raceId) | race_date: race date (derived from races.date) | points_in_race: total points that driver scored in that race (SUM(results.points) grouped by year, driverId, raceId) | running_season_points: cumulative SUM(points_in_race) OVER (PARTITION BY year, driverId ORDER BY race_date, raceId ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) — running total of points_in_race for the driver within the year up to and including that race
params.grounded_columns: results.driverId | results.raceId | results.points | races.raceId | races.date | races.year
params.metric: points_in_race = SUM(results.points) GROUP BY races.year, results.driverId, results.raceId, races.date | running_season_points = SUM(points_in_race) OVER (PARTITION BY year, driverId ORDER BY race_date, raceId ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
params.composition: Cardinality-SAFE joins (do not duplicate measures): |  - join to driver_dim on driver_dim.driverId = driver_running_points_by_season.driverId — safe because driver_running_points_by_season is one row per (year, driverId, raceId); joining to a driver dimension (one row per driver) will not multiply rows. |  - join to race_basic on race_basic.raceId = driver_running_points_by_season.raceId — safe because race_basic is one row per race. |  - join to constructor_dim only when joining via an equality that does not introduce multiplicity (e.g., when you first aggregate constructors to one row per constructor). Direct join on constructorId without ensuring one-to-one may be unsafe because this view has driver-level rows and constructors are not 1:1 with drivers across rows. |  | Do NOT join directly without care (these can multiply rows / duplicate measures unless you re-aggregate first): |  - race_results_enriched (JOIN) or any results-level table: these are typically one-to-many vs this view's (year, driverId, raceId) row — joining back to per-lap or per-stint rows (driver_lap_aggregates, pitstop_aggregates, race_results_enriched) will duplicate points_in_race and running_season_points unless you pre-aggregate the many-side to the same grain (year, driverId, raceId) or join on a strictly 1:1 key. |  - driver_lap_aggregates, pitstop_aggregates, fastest_lap_per_race, qualifying_grid_positions: these are many-per-race/per-driver or may be absent; aggregate them to (year, driverId, raceId) or to (raceId, driverId) and then join, or join and re-aggregate so you don't inflate running_season_points. |  | Composition recommendations for correctness: |  - If you need per-driver metrics from many-side tables (laps, pitstops), pre-aggregate those tables to the same grain (year, driverId, raceId) and then join on (year, driverId, raceId). That preserves the one-row-per-(year,driverId,raceId) property and avoids duplicating measures. |  - To compute final season points from this view, select MAX(running_season_points) GROUP BY year, driverId — this avoids relying on race-level joins. |  - To rank drivers at a particular race, filter by raceId (or race_date) and then apply RANK() over running_season_points partitioned by year.

Useful to plot championship progression race-by-race. | Use for: Plot championship points progression for a driver in a season; Determine points lead after each race

views.name: qualifying_attempts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  qualifyId,
  raceId,
  driverId,
  constructorId,
  number,
  position,
  q1,
  q2,
  q3,
  -- convert q1/q2/q3 like M:SS.mmm or SS.mmm to milliseconds where possible
  CASE
    WHEN q1 IS NULL OR trim(q1) = '' THEN NULL
    WHEN instr(q1, ':') > 0 THEN
      (CAST(substr(q1, 1, instr(q1, ':') - 1) AS INTEGER) * 60000)
      + CAST(REPLACE(substr(q1, instr(q1, ':') + 1), '.', '') AS INTEGER)
    ELSE
      CAST(REPLACE(q1, '.', '') AS INTEGER)
  END AS q1_ms,
  CASE
    WHEN q2 IS NULL OR trim(q2) = '' THEN NULL
    WHEN instr(q2, ':') > 0 THEN
      (CAST(substr(q2, 1, instr(q2, ':') - 1) AS INTEGER) * 60000)
      + CAST(REPLACE(substr(q2, instr(q2, ':') + 1), '.', '') AS INTEGER)
    ELSE
      CAST(REPLACE(q2, '.', '') AS INTEGER)
  END AS q2_ms,
  CASE
    WHEN q3 IS NULL OR trim(q3) = '' THEN NULL
    WHEN instr(q3, ':') > 0 THEN
      (CAST(substr(q3, 1, instr(q3, ':') - 1) AS INTEGER) * 60000)
      + CAST(REPLACE(substr(q3, instr(q3, ':') + 1), '.', '') AS INTEGER)
    ELSE
      CAST(REPLACE(q3, '.', '') AS INTEGER)
  END AS q3_ms
FROM qualifying
WHERE (q1 IS NOT NULL OR q2 IS NOT NULL OR q3 IS NOT NULL)
views.description: One row per qualifying attempt (driver in a race) with the recorded q1/q2/q3 times and related ids. Exposes raw qualifying time strings and numeric casts where possible for ordering.

views.name: qualifying_times_ms
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  qualifyId,
  raceId,
  driverId,
  -- parse q1/q2/q3 like "1:26.572" or "26.572" into milliseconds
  CASE
    WHEN q1 IS NULL OR trim(q1) = '' THEN NULL
    WHEN instr(q1, ':') > 0 THEN
      (
        -- minutes * 60 + seconds.millis -> ms
        (CAST(substr(q1, 1, instr(q1, ':') - 1) AS INTEGER) * 60 * 1000)
        +
        (CAST(
          -- seconds part may have fractional part; convert to float seconds then *1000
          replace(substr(q1, instr(q1, ':') + 1), ',', '.') AS REAL
        ) * 1000)
      )
    ELSE
      -- no minutes, treat as seconds.milliseconds
      (CAST(replace(q1, ',', '.') AS REAL) * 1000)
  END AS q1_ms,
  CASE
    WHEN q2 IS NULL OR trim(q2) = '' THEN NULL
    WHEN instr(q2, ':') > 0 THEN
      (
        (CAST(substr(q2, 1, instr(q2, ':') - 1) AS INTEGER) * 60 * 1000)
        +
        (CAST(replace(substr(q2, instr(q2, ':') + 1), ',', '.') AS REAL) * 1000)
      )
    ELSE
      (CAST(replace(q2, ',', '.') AS REAL) * 1000)
  END AS q2_ms,
  CASE
    WHEN q3 IS NULL OR trim(q3) = '' THEN NULL
    WHEN instr(q3, ':') > 0 THEN
      (
        (CAST(substr(q3, 1, instr(q3, ':') - 1) AS INTEGER) * 60 * 1000)
        +
        (CAST(replace(substr(q3, instr(q3, ':') + 1), ',', '.') AS REAL) * 1000)
      )
    ELSE
      (CAST(replace(q3, ',', '.') AS REAL) * 1000)
  END AS q3_ms
FROM qualifying
views.description: Normalized numeric milliseconds for qualifying segments (q1/q2/q3) parsed from time strings where possible to enable accurate ordering and comparisons.

SELECT

  driverId,
  q1,
  CASE
    WHEN q1 IS NULL OR trim(q1) = '' THEN NULL
    WHEN instr(q1, ':') > 0 THEN
      (CAST(substr(q1, 1, instr(q1, ':') - 1) AS INTEGER) * 60000)
      + CAST(
          (CASE
             WHEN instr(substr(q1, instr(q1, ':') + 1), '.') > 0
             THEN substr(substr(q1, instr(q1, ':') + 1), 1, instr(substr(q1, instr(q1, ':') + 1), '.') - 1)
             ELSE substr(q1, instr(q1, ':') + 1)
           END) AS INTEGER) * 1000
      + CAST(
          CASE
            WHEN instr(substr(q1, instr(q1, ':') + 1), '.') > 0
            THEN substr(substr(q1, instr(q1, ':') + 1), instr(substr(q1, instr(q1, ':') + 1), '.') + 1)
            ELSE '0'
          END AS INTEGER)
    ELSE
      -- no minutes part, assume seconds[.ms]
      (CAST(
         (CASE
            WHEN instr(q1, '.') > 0 THEN substr(q1, 1, instr(q1, '.') - 1)
            ELSE q1
          END) AS INTEGER) * 1000)
      + CAST(
          CASE
            WHEN instr(q1, '.') > 0 THEN substr(q1, instr(q1, '.') + 1)
            ELSE '0'
          END AS INTEGER)
  END AS q1_time_ms,
  q2,
  CASE
    WHEN q2 IS NULL OR trim(q2) = '' THEN NULL
    WHEN instr(q2, ':') > 0 THEN
      (CAST(substr(q2, 1, instr(q2, ':') - 1) AS INTEGER) * 60000)
      + CAST(

             ELSE substr(q2, instr(q2, ':') + 1)

      + CAST(
          CASE
            WHEN instr(substr(q2, instr(q2, ':') + 1), '.') > 0
            THEN substr(substr(q2, instr(q2, ':') + 1), instr(substr(q2, instr(q2, ':') + 1), '.') + 1)
            ELSE '0'
          END AS INTEGER)
    ELSE
      (CAST(
         (CASE
            WHEN instr(q2, '.') > 0 THEN substr(q2, 1, instr(q2, '.') - 1)
            ELSE q2
          END) AS INTEGER) * 1000)
      + CAST(
          CASE
            WHEN instr(q2, '.') > 0 THEN substr(q2, instr(q2, '.') + 1)
            ELSE '0'
          END AS INTEGER)
  END AS q2_time_ms,
  q3,
  CASE
    WHEN q3 IS NULL OR trim(q3) = '' THEN NULL
    WHEN instr(q3, ':') > 0 THEN
      (CAST(substr(q3, 1, instr(q3, ':') - 1) AS INTEGER) * 60000)

             THEN substr(substr(q3, instr(q3, ':') + 1), 1, instr(substr(q3, instr(q3, ':') + 1), '.') - 1)
             ELSE substr(q3, instr(q3, ':') + 1)
           END) AS INTEGER) * 1000
      + CAST(
          CASE
            WHEN instr(substr(q3, instr(q3, ':') + 1), '.') > 0
            THEN substr(substr(q3, instr(q3, ':') + 1), instr(substr(q3, instr(q3, ':') + 1), '.') + 1)

            WHEN instr(q3, '.') > 0 THEN substr(q3, 1, instr(q3, '.') - 1)

          END) AS INTEGER) * 1000)

views.name: numeric_fastest_lap_speed
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  results.resultId AS resultId,
  results.raceId AS raceId,
  results.driverId AS driverId,
  results.fastestLapSpeed AS fastestLapSpeed_raw,
  -- try to extract a numeric part (e.g. "218.300 km/h" or "218.300") using SQLite functions
  CASE
    WHEN results.fastestLapSpeed IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN trim(results.fastestLapSpeed) = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE
      -- Remove common unit strings and non-numeric trailing/leading chars, keep digits, dots and comma
      -- First replace comma with dot to normalize decimals
      -- Then strip any letters or slashes by keeping only characters 0-9 and dot via iterative removal
      -- SQLite lacks regexp, so perform a sequence of replacements for typical unit tokens, then remove non-dot/non-digit by translating unwanted chars to empty via nested replace for common letters.
      -- Finally, attempt CAST to numeric; if CAST yields 0 but original isn't zero, interpret as NULL by checking numeric validity with like pattern
      (CASE
        WHEN
          -- normalized string looks like a number (digits with optional one dot)
          (
            replace(
              replace(
                replace(
                  replace(
                    replace(
                      replace(
                        replace(
                          replace(
                            replace(
                              replace(
                                lower(trim(results.fastestLapSpeed)),
                                'km/h', ''
                              ),
                              'kph', ''
                            ),
                            'kmh', ''
                          ),
                          'km h', ''
                        ),
                        'k m/h', ''
                      ),
                      's', '' -- sometimes stray s
                    ),
                    'mph', ''
                  ),
                  'm/h', ''
                ),
                ',', '.'
              ),
              ' ', ''
            ) LIKE '%[^0-9.]%' ESCAPE '^' -- we will invert this check below
          )
        THEN
          -- If pattern check above indicates presence of non-numeric, attempt to strip letters by a safer sequence:
          CAST(
            replace(
              replace(
                replace(
                  replace(
                    replace(
                      replace(
                        replace(
                          replace(
                            replace(
                              replace(
                                replace(
                                  replace(
                                    replace(
                                      replace(
                                        replace(
                                          replace(
                                            replace(
                                              replace(
                                                replace(
                                                  replace(
                                                    replace(
                                                      replace(
                                                        replace(
                                                          replace(
                                                            lower(trim(results.fastestLapSpeed)),
                                                            'km/h',''
                                                          ),
                                                          'kph',''
                                                        ),
                                                        'kmh',''
                                                      ),
                                                      'km h',''
                                                    ),
                                                    'mph',''
                                                  ),
                                                  'm/h',''
                                                ),
                                                'speed',''
                                              ),
                                              'avg',''
                                            ),
                                            'average',''
                                          ),
                                          'max',''
                                        ),
                                        '(', ''
                                      ),
                                      ')', ''
                                    ),
                                    '+', ''
                                  ),
                                  '~', ''
                                ),
                                '/', ''
                              ),
                              '-', ''
                            ),
                            '--', ''
                          ),
                          ' ', ''
                        ),
                        ',', '.'
                      ),
                      'a', ''
                    ),
                    'b', ''
                  ),
                  'c', ''
                ),
                'd', ''
              ),
              'e', ''
            ) AS REAL
          )
        ELSE
          -- simple normalized numeric cast
          CAST(
            replace(
              replace(lower(trim(results.fastestLapSpeed)), 'km/h',''),
              ',', '.'
            ) AS REAL
          )
      END)
  END AS fastestLapSpeed_numeric
FROM results
WHERE results.fastestLapSpeed IS NOT NULL
  AND trim(results.fastestLapSpeed) != ''
  -- Exclude rows where numeric conversion would yield NULL: ensure after basic normalization there's at least one digit
  AND (
    replace(
      replace(lower(trim(results.fastestLapSpeed)), 'km/h',''),
      ',', '.'
    ) LIKE '%0%' OR replace(
      replace(lower(trim(results.fastestLapSpeed)), 'km/h',''),
      ',', '.'
    ) LIKE '%1%' OR replace(
      replace(lower(trim(results.fastestLapSpeed)), 'km/h',''),
      ',', '.'
    ) LIKE '%2%' OR replace(
      replace(lower(trim(results.fastestLapSpeed)), 'km/h',''),
      ',', '.'
    ) LIKE '%3%' OR replace(
      replace(lower(trim(results.fastestLapSpeed)), 'km/h',''),
      ',', '.'
    ) LIKE '%4%' OR replace(
      replace(lower(trim(results.fastestLapSpeed)), 'km/h',''),
      ',', '.'
    ) LIKE '%5%' OR replace(
      replace(lower(trim(results.fastestLapSpeed)), 'km/h',''),
      ',', '.'
    ) LIKE '%6%' OR replace(
      replace(lower(trim(results.fastestLapSpeed)), 'km/h',''),
      ',', '.'
    ) LIKE '%7%' OR replace(
      replace(lower(trim(results.fastestLapSpeed)), 'km/h',''),
      ',', '.'
    ) LIKE '%8%' OR replace(
      replace(lower(trim(results.fastestLapSpeed)), 'km/h',''),
      ',', '.'
    ) LIKE '%9%'
  )
grain: resultId -- one row per results.resultId with an attempted numeric fastest lap speed
views.description: Normalized projection of results.fastestLapSpeed parsed to a numeric value (km/h or numeric part) and exposes status if present. Keeps original text and numeric conversion; excludes rows where conversion fails.

views.name: race_fastest_lap_speed_by_driver
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.resultId,
  r.raceId,
  r.driverId,
  MAX(
    CASE
      WHEN r.fastestLapSpeed IS NULL THEN NULL
      WHEN trim(r.fastestLapSpeed) = '' THEN NULL
      ELSE
        CAST(
          REPLACE(
            REPLACE(r.fastestLapSpeed, 'km/h', ''),
            'kph', ''
          ) AS REAL
        )
    END
  ) AS max_fastestLapSpeed_numeric
FROM results r
GROUP BY r.raceId, r.driverId, r.resultId
views.description: Per race (and optionally per driver) best (max) numeric fastest lap speed observed in results. Useful to compare fastest lap speeds across races or drivers. Keeps source raceId and driverId for filtering.

views.body_sql:

  results rr
ON
  r.raceId = rr.raceId

views.description: Aggregated per-race participation measures: total participants and count of participants with a non-empty time value. Keeps raceId as the grouping key so callers can join to race_core and compute completion rate.

views.name: drivers_dim
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.driverId AS driverId,
  d.driverRef AS driverRef,
  TRIM(d.forename) AS forename,

  TRIM(
    COALESCE(d.forename, '') || CASE WHEN d.forename IS NOT NULL AND d.surname IS NOT NULL THEN ' ' ELSE '' END || COALESCE(d.surname, '')

  d.number AS number,
  d.code AS code,
  d.dob AS dob,

views.name: drivers_with_fullname
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.driverId,
  d.forename,
  d.surname,
  -- compute full_name: prefer "forename surname", handle NULLs
  CASE
    WHEN d.forename IS NOT NULL AND d.surname IS NOT NULL THEN trim(d.forename || ' ' || d.surname)
    WHEN d.forename IS NOT NULL THEN trim(d.forename)
    WHEN d.surname IS NOT NULL THEN trim(d.surname)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS full_name,
  -- normalize dob to ISO DATE (stored as DATE in schema); pass through as dob for presentation
  d.dob AS dob,
  d.nationality
FROM drivers d
views.description: Driver rows augmented with a single computed full name string and normalized dob for straightforward presentation and selection.

views.name: driver_age_candidates
views.body_sql:

  d.forename AS forename,
  d.surname AS surname,
  d.dob AS dob,

FROM drivers AS d
WHERE d.dob IS NOT NULL
